The five rules

The Bushido Code of Summarising

Before an apprentice touches a single story, they learn what a summary is for. These five rules hang on the dojo wall — every rank, every lesson, every scroll.

    The one blade every apprentice carries

    The S.W.O.R.D. method

    Not a weapon of steel — a weapon of attention. Five moves, drawn in order, on every single story from lesson one to lesson eighty. Tap a letter.

    Ten lessons per rank

    Eight ranks, one path

    Every rank hands the student a little less help than the one before it — until the final belt asks for none at all.

    See it for yourself

    Story one: the full five-lesson cycle

    Every one of the forty stories now takes five lessons: read the whole thing once, summarise it one paragraph at a time using the S.W.O.R.D. method, then bring all three summaries together. Switch between the five lessons below to see the whole cycle for Story 1 — Creation.

    Rank one · Apprentice Samurai · white belt · Story 1 of 40

    Lesson 1 of 5: Creation — Read & Understand

    About 15 minutes No summarising yet
    Katana warm-upThe scrollComprehension checkRetell itMaster's seal
    1Katana warm-up1–2 min
    Welcome, apprentice. Before you ever learn to summarise a story, you have to truly understand it — that's rule one of the Bushido Code: honour the truth.

    So today's lesson has no sword-work at all. Just read the story of how everything began, start to finish, and make sure it makes sense. Next lesson, you'll draw the S.W.O.R.D. for the first time — on just the first paragraph.
    2The scroll4–5 min

    Every story in the dojo is written on three scrolls, so every apprentice can read at their own level — and every scroll is written in the same three paragraphs: a beginning, a middle, and an end. Try switching between the scrolls — notice how the story never changes, only how it's told. Read all three paragraphs before moving on.

    3Comprehension check4–5 min

    No summarising yet — just check that you followed the story. (Drawing the SWORD starts next lesson, on paragraph 1 alone.)

    Who is this story about?

    Tap the words that name a character in the story, not a place or a thing.

    What happened, and in what order?

    Tap the four events in the order they happen in the story.

    True or false?

    Tap the statements that are actually true in the story.

    4Retell it2–3 min

    Tell the story back in your own words, like you're explaining it to a friend who's never heard it. Take as long as you like — this isn't a summary yet, so don't worry about cutting anything out. That's what the next three lessons are for.

    0 words

    5Master's seal1 min

    Check your understanding against the three questions every apprentice asks before rolling up the scroll.

    • Do I know who the story is about?
    • Do I know what happened at the beginning, middle, and end?
    • Could I explain the whole story to someone else?
    ⛩️

    Lesson 2 of 5: Creation — Draw the Sword: The Beginning

    About 15 minutesFirst S.W.O.R.D. of the story
    Katana warm-upRe-read paragraph 1Draw the S.W.O.R.D.Dojo challengeSelf-check
    1Katana warm-up1–2 min
    Welcome back, apprentice. Last lesson you read the whole story of Creation and made sure you understood it. Today, for the very first time, you'll draw the S.W.O.R.D. — but only on the first paragraph, the Beginning.

    Quick recall: what does the S in S.W.O.R.D. stand for? (It's always the very first move.)
    2Re-read paragraph 11 min

    Read paragraph 1 — the Beginning — once more, closely this time. You can still switch reading levels; it's the same paragraph, just told differently.

    3Draw the S.W.O.R.D.5–7 min

    Work through all five moves, one at a time, using just paragraph 1.

    S · Search — who is in this paragraph?

    Tap the word that names a character — not a place or a thing.

    W · Watch, O · Order — what happens, and when?

    Tap these four events in the order they happen in paragraph 1.

    R · Remove — what can be cut?

    Tap the phrases that could be left out of a summary without losing the meaning.

    D · Deliver — say it in your own words

    Fill in the gaps to build your own sentence.

    First, God made and , then .
    4Dojo challenge2–3 min

    Now write it as one clean sentence — your own summary of paragraph 1 only.

    0 words

    5Quick self-check1 min

    Before you roll the scroll back up:

    • Did I only keep what matters from paragraph 1?
    • Is it in my own words, not copied from the scroll?

    Lesson 5 of 5: Creation — The Full Scroll

    About 15 minutesBringing it together
    Your three swordsCombine & polishBushido checklistMaster's seal
    1Your three S.W.O.R.D.s1–2 min

    Here are the three sentences you drew in Lessons 2, 3 and 4. Read them together, in order.

    2Combine & polish4–5 min

    Turn your three sentences into one smooth, 2–4 sentence summary of the whole story. Cut anything that repeats, and smooth the joins between them.

    0 words

    3Bushido checklist1–2 min

    Check your finished summary against the Code, one rule at a time.

    • Honour the truth — does it say only what the story says?
    • Discipline to cut — did I leave out what doesn't matter?
    • Clarity is strength — could someone understand it in one read?
    • Speak with your own voice — is it in my own words?
    4Master's seal1 min

    Story 1 of 40, complete.
